# Finite-base entropy escorts and an exact failure of their maximizing center

This note characterizes the proposed BASE-mean entropy selector and then
falsifies its OC guarantee on an actual three-fiber convex body. The exact
example was found by Two-sided and independently checked by the contributor and
Defect. It does not refute OC or the ordinary joint Minkowski concavity
of projective volume energy.

## 1. Exact finite characterization

Let P be a finite occupied integer base set, K_z its d-dimensional convex
body fibers, v_z=|K_z|>0, and g_z their ordinary centroids. Fix d>=1 and
p in P. Put D=d+2 and q=(D-1)/D. Consider the entropy value

    B(p)=sup (integral_S rho^q dmu)^D,

where mu is the original mixed volume measure, rho>=0, integral rho=1,
and the probability's base mean is p; its continuous mean is FREE.
Let F be the minimal face of conv P containing p, and write P_F=P cap F.
Every feasible probability is supported on these bases: a supporting
hyperplane for F has zero expected nonnegative gap. Within each fiber,
Jensen shows that the unique maximizing density is constant. Thus

    B(p)=max [sum_(z in P_F) v_z^(1/D) pi_z^q]^D,        (1)

subject to pi_z>=0, sum pi_z=1, sum pi_z z=p. There is a unique optimal
pi, because the displayed sum before taking its positive power is
strictly concave. All its entries on P_F are positive. Indeed p is in
the relative interior of F, so a feasible pi with every entry positive
exists; mixing it into an alleged optimum with a zero entry has gain
of order t^q and loss of order t, contradicting optimality for small t.

The Lagrange equations, restricted to the affine span of F, give an
affine function

    L_z=1+alpha.(z-p)>0,

and the exact formulas

    pi_z=v_z L_z^(-D)/B(p),
    sum v_z L_z^(-D)=sum v_z L_z^(-(D-1))=B(p),
    sum v_z(z-p)L_z^(-D)=0.                            (2)

For clarity, if S0=sum v_z^(1/D)pi_z^q, multiplication of the Lagrange
equations by pi_z shows their constant multiplier is q S0. Dividing
by q S0 gives L_z above and pi_z=v_z/(S0^D L_z^D); the mean constraint
and sum pi_z L_z=1 prove all normalizations in(2).
Equivalently, Hölder and(2) give the exact face-restricted dual

    B(p)=min_alpha sum_(z in P_F)
                       v_z[1+alpha.(z-p)]^(-d-1).       (3)

The minimum is attained on the relative parameter space of this face.
For boundary p, formula(3) is not an assertion of finite attainment of
an unrestricted all-base dual: bases outside F are absent here.

The selected continuous mean is

    y_p=sum pi_z g_z.                                  (4)

Actual convex fiber compatibility implies y_p is in int K_p: the
Minkowski combination sum pi_z K_z has nonempty interior and is
contained in K_p, and its combined centroid point has an interior
ball supplied by the positive input coefficients. This uses an actual
convex family, not arbitrary mass/centroid arrays.

The proposed rule is to maximize B(p) over occupied integer bases and
choose (p,y_p). Section3 shows that this rule can fail the OC target.

## 2. Closed formula for three consecutive fibers

For bases -1,0,1 write their volumes a,c,b and centroids g_-,g_0,g_+.
At the extreme bases the escort is supported on its own fiber, so
B(-1)=a and B(1)=b. At p=0 put

    A=a^(1/D), B=b^(1/D),
    alpha=(B-A)/(B+A),
    w=((A+B)/2)^D.

Then the two endpoint unnormalized escort masses agree exactly:

    a/(1-alpha)^D=b/(1+alpha)^D=w.

Consequently

    B(0)=c+2w,
    y_0=[c g_0+w(g_-+g_+)]/(c+2w).                     (5)

In particular equal endpoint masses give the ordinary mixed centroid.
No halfspace-depth lower bound follows merely from(5).

## 3. Exact actual counterexample

In R^2 let

    T=conv{(2,-1),(-1,2),(-1,-1)},  V=|T|=9/2,
    A=T, K=3T, B=4T,
    C=conv[{-1} times A, {0} times K, {1} times B].

The three integer fibers of C are exactly A,K,B. Endpoint fibers are
extreme in the base, and (A+B)/2=(5/2)T is contained in3T. Thus anchored
endpoint interpolation adds nothing to the prescribed middle fiber.
The body is compact, full dimensional, and has precisely these three
positive-area integer fibers. Its original mass is

    M=(1+9+16)V=26V.                                   (6)

All three fiber centroids are0, so the centroid graph is affine. Taking
d=2, D=4, the middle parameter in(5) is alpha=1/3 and

    w=(3/2)^4 V=81V/16,
    B(0)=9V+2(81V/16)=153V/8,
    pi_-=pi_+=9/34,  pi_0=8/17.

Thus B(0)>B(1)=16V>B(-1)=V: the maximizing base is UNIQUE, and the
proposed selected point is exactly Y=(0,0,0).

The closed ambient halfspace

    H={ (z,x): x_1-8z>=0 }

contains Y on its boundary. At base -1 its threshold is -8, so it
contains all of T. At base0 it cuts3T by x_1>=0, a similar triangle
whose area is(2/3)^2|3T|=4V. At base1 its threshold is8, the maximum
of x_1 on4T, so its intersection is a single vertex and has area0.
Hence the ACTUAL mixed cap mass is

    mu(S cap H)=V+4V+0=5V.

The required OC raw target here is

    (Gamma_2/2)M=(2/9)26V=52V/9>5V.                    (7)

Therefore the depth of the unique entropy-selected point is at most
5/26<2/9. There is no tie-breaking ambiguity and no unsupported claim
of criticality of this particular cap: one actual containing cap is
enough to disprove the selector's guarantee.

The original body is separately OC-safe. At the actual point(1,0,0),
every containing ambient halfspace with nonzero continuous normal
captures at least Gamma_2|B|=64V/9 in its OWN fiber, by the ordinary
centroid inequality. Pure-integer containing halfspaces capture all
of B. Thus this point has raw depth at least64V/9>52V/9. The failure
is entirely the proposed base/escort selection rule, not existence.

## 4. Information retained and stopping rule

The selector uses only fiber masses and ordinary centroids; even an
affine centroid graph does not repair its wrong choice of base. The
ordinary projective energy E_(K_p)(y), its marked homothety equality,
and its joint Minkowski concavity are different objects and remain
valid. No new all-base entropy-center guarantee is proposed here.
The d=200 all-template obstruction is unnecessary to falsify this
candidate, because the rational planar homothetic family already does.
